--- title: "[Graph.degrees()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get degree for all nodes in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13531-L13615){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.degrees(attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For directed graphs, returns total degree (in-degree + out-degree). For undirected graphs, returns the number of neighbors. This batch method is more efficient than calling get_degree() for each node individually and automatically stores results in the node DataFrame. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store degree values in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `degree`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to degree values. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Compute degrees for all nodes: ::: {#28f86b2c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("A", "C") .degrees(return_dict=False) # Stores in 'degree' column, returns self ) # Access via node DataFrame ndf = graph.get_node_df() # Returns DataFrame with id and degree columns ndf.select(["id", "degree"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
